## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

subject_definitions:
<Video 1> is the source video being edited, providing the outdoor park setting, the performers' dramatic acting and embracing motion, composition, camera movement, and timing.
<Subject 1> is the target male character whose facial identity, hairstyle, clothing (blue and gold ancient-style robe with shoulder armor), and accessories come from <Picture 1>. This character replaces only the short-haired man in the black suit visible in <Video 1>.
<Subject 2> is the target female character whose facial identity, hairstyle, clothing (blue and white ancient-style dress with gold shoulder armor and hair ornaments), and accessories come from <Picture 2>. This character replaces only the woman in the black top and jeans with a flower in her hair visible in <Video 1>.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation + audio reuse] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. Replace the man with <Subject 1> and the woman with <Subject 2>, preserve the original outdoor environment and visual style, remove overlaid subtitles and video watermarks, and fully reuse the original synchronized audio track in synchronization with the source.

retention_analysis:
<Video 1> (throughout the clip): partially_preserved - replace the performers' appearances and remove overlaid subtitles and video watermarks while preserving their visible dramatic acting, embracing performance, the outdoor park environment, composition, camera movement, and event order.
<Subject 1> (throughout the clip): fully_preserved - retain the target identity and appearance defined by <Picture 1>, adapted to the source poses, expressions (especially the hoarse and desperate facial expressions), viewpoints, and lighting.
<Subject 2> (throughout the clip): fully_preserved - retain the target identity and appearance defined by <Picture 2>, adapted to the source poses, expressions (especially the shy and charming facial expressions), viewpoints, and lighting.
Original audio track: fully_copy - reuse the complete synchronized source soundtrack as the target video's complete final audio track without trimming, replacement, or added sound layers.

detailed_description:
The target video retains the source's live-action appearance, natural daylight, color treatment, and camera texture.
[Shot 1] A continuous medium shot captures a man and a woman in an outdoor park setting with trees and bamboo in the background. Replace the short-haired man in the black suit with <Subject 1> and the woman in the black top and jeans with a flower in her hair with <Subject 2>, matching their faces, hairstyles, and ancient-style clothing shown in <Picture 1> and <Picture 2> respectively. Adapt them naturally to the source actors' head turns, strides, arm swings, and changing view angles. Keep them in the same screen positions and preserve the exact same acting pace and direction. The camera tracks alongside them at the source speed and distance. Strictly preserve the man's hoarse, desperate, and exaggerated facial expressions and the woman's shy, charming, and slightly resistant expressions exactly as they occur in the source footage. Maintain the physical contact, embracing, pulling, and holding poses between the two characters exactly as in the source video, including all visible limb contacts, waist holding, and collar grabbing. Remove the overlaid white Chinese subtitles at the bottom and the platform watermark in the top right corner, naturally reconstructing the covered character or background details with temporal consistency. Do not crop, zoom, blur, cover, or add a replacement mark to conceal them; retain real signs or writing physically present in the environment. Do not add another person, a new prop, a new action, a cut, or a change of location. The synced original dialogue, singing, and ambient sounds continue at their source timing through the final frame.

overall_soundscape:
The original outdoor ambience, vocal sounds, clothing rustles, and physical interaction sounds from the source audio remain synchronized with the source interval.

non_diegetic_music:
The original music and vocal layers from the source audio are reused in full at their source timing and level.
